criteria.description: Integer-type validation and docstring examples: correctly returns False when any of x,y,z is not an int (e.g., float like 3.6, -2.2) and returns True/False matching the 4 docstring examples when all are ints. A crash or non-termination on these inputs is severe.

Sum condition logic: when all three are ints, returns True iff x==y+z or y==x+z or z==x+y. Must handle zero (e.g., 0,0,0 -> True; 0,1,1 -> True) and negatives (e.g., 3,-2,1 -> True) correctly. Wrong boolean on rare case is moderate; crash is severe.

Implementation validity and robustness: the returned body is syntactically valid Python, first line indentation fits the function, no infinite loop, and does not crash on numeric inputs including large values, negatives, and zero. Returns a bool in all paths.
